classification_note: Stage 01's saved runtime reports `AddressSanitizer: use-after-poison READ of size 1` because AFL stores the testcase in a larger malloc-backed slab and poisons bytes past the logical input length. Source-grounded analysis and the staged fix show the underlying project bug is a one-byte out-of-bounds read past the 7-byte MQTT datagram.

bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer at `src/mqtt.c:69` while the staged fuzz harness called `mg_mqtt_parse(data, size, 5, &mm)` on the exact 7-byte witness `30 05 00 00 ff ff ff`. In `mg_mqtt_parse`, byte 0 decodes to `MQTT_CMD_PUBLISH` with `qos == 0`, byte 1 decodes remaining length `n = 5`, and `end = buf + 7` therefore limits the logical datagram to the exact 7 testcase bytes. The PUBLISH parser then reads a zero topic length from bytes 2-3, so `p` advances to `buf + 4`; the separate `if (m->qos > 0)` branch is not taken, so no packet-id bytes are consumed and only the three trailing bytes `ff ff ff` remain before `end`. Because `version == 5` and `p + 2 < end` still hold, the vulnerable code calls `decode_variable_length((char *) p, &len_len)` on that 3-byte suffix. All three remaining bytes keep the MQTT continuation bit set, but vulnerable `decode_variable_length()` has no remaining-length parameter and loops only on `offset < 4`, so it attempts a fourth `p[offset]` read at `p[3]`, one byte past the datagram. The saved ASan report surfaces that read as `use-after-poison READ of size 1`; the staged fix replaces the helper with length-aware `decode_varint(buf, end - p, &value)` and rejects truncated varints with `MQTT_MALFORMED` instead of reading past `end`.

source.description: First project-side decode of the raw witness bytes. The MQTT fixed-header byte is split into the command and QoS fields that select the PUBLISH parser arm and its QoS-gated packet-id handling.
source.value_from: Step 1 passes the exact 7-byte witness into `mg_mqtt_parse(data, size, 5, &mm)`. Inside `mg_mqtt_parse`, the first project read of that buffer is `buf[0]`; for this witness it is `0x30`, which decodes to `MQTT_CMD_PUBLISH` with QoS 0.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: This QoS-gated packet-id branch is the final project-side decision that determines where the MQTT v5 properties-length varint begins.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Step 4 advances `p` to `buf + 4` after decoding a zero-length topic, and step 2 set `m->qos == 0` from header byte `0x30`. Therefore the branch at lines 392-396 is skipped, no packet-id bytes are consumed, and the remaining three bytes `ff ff ff` become the entire input to `decode_variable_length`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. On the fourth varint iteration, the helper reads one byte past the 7-byte MQTT datagram.
sink.note: The saved Stage 01 trace reports `AddressSanitizer: use-after-poison READ of size 1` at `src/mqtt.c:69:20` in `decode_variable_length`; source-level analysis shows that read is `p[3]` when only `p[0..2]` exist after the QoS-0 branch leaves `p` at `buf + 4`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The MQTT variable-length decoder is bounded only by the protocol maximum of four bytes and has no caller-supplied remaining length, so it never proves that another byte is still inside the packet before reading `p[offset]`.
root_cause.note: The staged fix confirms the missing obligation by replacing this helper with `decode_varint(const uint8_t *buf, size_t len, size_t *value)` and changing the loop condition to `offset < 4 && offset < len`, returning failure when the varint is truncated.

parser_admitted.description: After the fixed header and zero-length topic are accepted and the QoS-gated packet-id branch is skipped, the saved witness reaches the MQTT v5 properties parser. For this input the branch is taken with `p == buf + 4` and `end == buf + 7`, so the parser enters varint decoding even though only three bytes remain.

evidence_limitations: Stage 02 did not dynamically validate the fixed image; `patch_resolves: true` is source-grounded from `patch.diff` plus the saved vulnerable run, not from a vulnerable-versus-fixed execution pair.

The saved detector context is the AFL driver's poisoned testcase slab rather than a malloc owned by Mongoose itself, so ASan names the fault `use-after-poison`. The project-side bug is still a one-byte read past the logical 7-byte MQTT datagram.

fine_trace.note: The reproducing harness call feeds the exact 7-byte witness to the MQTT parser with `version == 5`, which is the only mode that treats post-topic bytes as a properties-length varint.
Source. The first witness byte `0x30` is decoded into `m->cmd == MQTT_CMD_PUBLISH` and `m->qos == 0`, selecting the PUBLISH parser arm and setting up the later QoS branch to skip packet-id parsing.

fine_trace.var: lc, n, len_len, p, end, m->dgram.len
fine_trace.note: The second witness byte `0x05` becomes the MQTT remaining length `n = 5` with `len_len = 1`. Since `p` is now `buf + 2`, the parser sets `end = buf + 7` and `m->dgram.len = 7`, which defines the exact packet extent every later bounds check should respect.
Bytes 2-3 are `00 00`, so `m->topic.len` becomes 0 and `p` advances from `buf + 2` to `buf + 4`. After this move, exactly the three trailing bytes `ff ff ff` lie between `p` and `end`.

The QoS-gated packet-id branch is not taken because step 2 set `m->qos == 0`. No packet-id bytes are consumed, so `p` stays at `buf + 4` and the same three-byte suffix `ff ff ff` remains between `p` and `end` when control reaches the MQTT v5 properties parser.

This is the only admission check before decoding the MQTT v5 properties-length field. For the witness, `version == 5`, `p == buf + 4`, and `end == buf + 7`, so the branch is taken and `decode_variable_length((char *) p, &len_len)` is invoked on a suffix that is only 3 bytes long.

On its first three iterations, the helper reads `p[0]`, `p[1]`, and `p[2]`, which are all `0xff`. Each byte keeps the MQTT continuation bit set, so the break condition never fires and the decode still expects another byte after consuming the entire 3-byte suffix.

Root cause. The loop is bounded only by `offset < 4`; the helper receives no remaining-length argument and never checks `offset < end - p`. After step 7 keeps the continuation bit set for the first three bytes, this loop still permits a fourth iteration even though the suffix at `p` is only 3 bytes long.

Sink. On the fourth iteration (`offset == 3`), `p[3]` is one byte past the 7-byte datagram because only `p[0..2]` exist after step 5 leaves `p == buf + 4`. That read triggers the saved AddressSanitizer `use-after-poison READ of size 1` at `src/mqtt.c:69`, which corresponds source-level to a one-byte out-of-bounds read past the logical MQTT packet.

format.name: 7-byte MQTT v5 PUBLISH packet with a truncated properties-length varint
format.contract: Exactly the 7-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_58319/poc` (sha256 `26ede6f569984a7158280739c7b4124a7d5b977ca66fd810aae4dd7c6e680bc7`): `30 05 00 00 ff ff ff`. `mg_mqtt_parse(data, size, 5, &mm)` reads byte 0 as the MQTT fixed header (`cmd = PUBLISH`, `qos = 0`), byte 1 as remaining length `0x05`, bytes 2-3 as zero topic length, and bytes 4-6 as a three-byte truncated MQTT v5 properties-length varint whose continuation bits all remain set. Those exact staged values make `p == buf + 4`, `end == buf + 7`, satisfy `version == 5 && p + 2 < end`, and force vulnerable `decode_variable_length()` to attempt a fourth read from `p[3]` past the end of the datagram.
